Deep Chlorophyll Maximum (DCM)
A near-universal feature of stratified tropical and subtropical oceans. The DCM forms where photosynthetically active radiation (PAR) attenuates to a level just sufficient for net photosynthesis while nitrate-rich water from depth becomes available — the intersection of the euphotic zone and the nitracline. Phytoplankton aggregate at this optimal depth, producing a sharp subsurface peak in chlorophyll fluorescence typically between 50–150 m, well below the mixed layer.
Two mechanisms drive the DCM: photoacclimation (DAM — cells produce more pigment per cell in dim light, chlorophyll rises but BBP stays flat) and biomass accumulation (DBM — true cell proliferation where upwelled nutrients intersect available light; chlorophyll and BBP co-peak).
Data & Indicators
Vertical profiles — BGC-Argo autonomous floats: chlorophyll (CHL), temperature (TEMP), salinity (SAL), dissolved oxygen (O₂), nitrate (NO₃), and particulate backscattering (BBP) sampled continuously from surface to 1000 m.
Surface chlorophyll — Ocean Colour CCI v2 (OCCCI v2) monthly satellite climatology. A merged, bias-corrected multi-sensor product providing a stable reference for near-surface phytoplankton pigment across the Indian Ocean.
PAR — MODIS Aqua monthly climatology (mol photons m⁻² d⁻¹), used as a proxy for surface light forcing controlling the depth of the euphotic zone.

MLD — Mixed Layer Depth: base of the wind-mixed surface layer where temperature, salinity, and nutrients are homogenized. Below MLD the water stratifies and phytoplankton rely on upward nutrient diffusion.
Nitracline — Depth where nitrate rises sharply, marking the top of the subsurface nutrient reservoir. The DCM typically sits just above or at this horizon where nutrient supply meets residual light.
26°C isotherm — Depth of the 26°C temperature surface, a standard thermocline proxy for tropical oceans. Seasonal shoaling of this surface compresses the euphotic zone and shifts DCM position.

[DCM]

The Deep Chlorophyll Maximum is a ubiquitous subsurface feature of stratified ocean basins. It forms where photosynthetically active radiation intersects with the nitracline, creating optimal conditions for phytoplankton accumulation well below the mixed layer.

[DAM]

The Deep Acclimation Maximum is a photoacclimation artifact: phytoplankton cells increase pigment content per unit biomass in response to low light below the mixed layer. Chlorophyll peaks sharply at depth while backscatter (BBP) remains low or flat — pigment, not biomass, is elevated.

[DBM]

The Deep Biomass Maximum reflects a true increase in phytoplankton biomass at depth, where nutrients from below the pycnocline intersect with sufficient light. Chlorophyll and BBP co-peak, confirming that cell abundance — not just pigment — is elevated. Dominates in nutrient-rich and seasonally mixed regimes.
